ALIAS PAIRS REQUIRING MERGE, NOT DELETION. Five domain ids in the wave-1 corpus are near-synonyms of others and were defined here so no edge dangles, but a merge pass should decide a canonical for each: d-legislative / d-legislation (process vs enacted text); d-funding / d-money (channel vs opacity); d-secrecy / d-secrecy-architecture (law vs compartment topology); d-contractor / d-contracting (custody vs acquisition mechanics); d-ffrdc / d-ffrdc-mechanism (institution vs FAR 35.017 clause). Each pair is written here with a deliberate division of labour so both can survive if the board prefers granularity.

FOUR DOMAIN IDS WERE ALREADY DEFINED ELSEWHERE AND WERE NOT REDEFINED HERE: d-ffrdc and d-structure and d-media (in media-structure.json and ffrdcs.json) and d-custody (in scientists-technical.json). d-materials WAS redefined here because it appears in the required list; scientists-technical.json also carries a definition and the two must be reconciled rather than both loaded. Note also that media-structure.json defines a domain with the bare id 'ffrdc-mechanism' while one record references 'd-ffrdc-mechanism' - a prefix inconsistency the merge pass should normalise.

NINE DOMAINS ARE DEFINED FORWARD, NOT BACKWARD. d-intel, d-nuc, d-plasma, d-chem, d-consciousness, d-remote-viewing, d-signals, d-aerospace and d-counterintel are not yet referenced by any wave-1 person record. They were in the required list and are defined here for wave-2 and wave-3 scoring. Until people are scored on them they carry no graph weight, and a later pass should backfill domains[] on existing person records - the aviators dossier in particular should almost certainly carry d-signals, and the scientists dossier d-chem and d-astro.

THE C AXIS IS UNDER-EVIDENCED ON EXACTLY THE DOMAINS THAT MATTER MOST. d-legacy, d-recovery, d-reverse-engineering and d-bio are scored C3 on the strength of sworn testimony (tier 2) rather than primary documents (tier 1).
